Product Team · Meeting Notes

Sprint Planning — Sprint 24

Monday, November 23, 2026 10:00–11:30 a.m. PT Room Atlas / Zoom Facilitator: Priya Nair

1. Attendees

Nine of ten invited people attended. Engineering lead Jordan Hale joined the last 20 minutes for capacity confirmation.

Priya Nair · PM, facilitator Marcus Chen · Design Aisha Rahman · Engineering Leo Park · Engineering Sam Okonkwo · QA Elena Voss · Data Chris Alvarez · Support Jordan Hale · Eng lead (partial)

Absent: Nina Patel (on leave). Notes will be shared with her before standup tomorrow.

2. Agenda

  1. Sprint 23 review and carryover (10 min)
  2. Sprint goal and success metrics (10 min)
  3. Candidate backlog and sizing (35 min)
  4. Capacity, risks, and dependencies (15 min)
  5. Commitment, owners, and open questions (15 min)

3. Discussion

3.1 Sprint 23 review and carryover

Sprint 23 closed at 28 of 34 committed points. The billing-export job and the saved-filters polish both slipped after a late dependency on the payments vendor sandbox. Support volume on the export path stayed elevated (about 40 tickets last week), so carryover is treated as customer-visible, not optional cleanup.

  • Carry into Sprint 24: CSV export reliability (BILL-412) and saved-filter persistence (SEARCH-188).
  • Drop from the candidate list: dark-mode token cleanup. Design confirmed it can wait until the design-system release in December.
  • Sam flagged two flaky end-to-end tests that masked a real export failure. QA will stabilize those before new export work merges.

3.2 Sprint goal and success metrics

Priya proposed a single goal: make recurring exports trustworthy enough that support tickets on that path fall by half, and ship the first version of team-shared saved views. The group accepted the goal with one change — shared views stay behind a feature flag until Elena confirms the analytics events are firing correctly.

Success for the sprint is defined as:

  • Export job success rate at or above 99% in staging for three consecutive days.
  • Support tickets tagged “export failed” down at least 50% versus the Sprint 23 weekly average by the end of the sprint.
  • Shared saved views available to the internal beta cohort, flagged off in production.

3.3 Candidate backlog and sizing

The team walked the top of the backlog and sized only items that could fit the goal. Points are planning poker consensus, not individual estimates.

  • BILL-412 — Retry and alert on failed exports (5 pts). Aisha owns the retry policy. Leo will add the failure webhook so Support sees a ticket reason instead of a silent miss. Chris asked that the customer-facing error name the file and the time, not a generic “try again.”
  • SEARCH-188 — Persist saved filters across sessions (3 pts). Carryover. Marcus has the empty and error states ready. Small scope; do not expand into sharing.
  • SEARCH-201 — Team-shared saved views, v1 (8 pts). Create, rename, and revoke only. No permissions matrix this sprint. Elena needs an event for view-created, view-applied, and view-revoked before the flag can open to the beta cohort.
  • PLAT-77 — Fix flaky export e2e tests (2 pts). Sam. Prerequisite for BILL-412 merge.
  • Not committed: mobile filter sheet redesign (SEARCH-210, 8 pts) and admin audit log (ADMIN-54, 5 pts). Both stay in the backlog. Audit log was close; Jordan said platform capacity is already spoken for by the vendor sandbox follow-up.

3.4 Capacity, risks, and dependencies

Available capacity is 22 points after accounting for a company holiday on Thursday, November 26, and Aisha’s half-day onboarding shadow on Friday. Committed scope is 18 points, leaving a small buffer.

  • Vendor sandbox. Payments confirmed the sandbox reset lands Wednesday. BILL-412 cannot be verified end to end before that. Aisha will stub the failure path so development is not blocked.
  • Holiday coverage. No deploys Thursday or Friday. Last production deploy window this sprint is Wednesday, December 2, pending the usual release checklist.
  • Analytics. Shared views stay flagged off until Elena signs off on the three events. If instrumentation slips, the UI still ships internally; the flag does not open.
  • Support load. Chris will keep a daily export-ticket count in the sprint channel so the 50% target is visible, not discovered at review.

3.5 Commitment

The team committed to BILL-412, SEARCH-188, SEARCH-201, and PLAT-77, totaling 18 points, against the goal above. Sprint 24 runs Monday, November 23 through Friday, December 4, with no deploy on the holiday or the day after. Review is scheduled for Thursday, December 3 at 2:00 p.m. PT.

4. Decisions

  1. Sprint goal accepted. Recurring exports become reliable enough to cut related support tickets by about half, and team-shared saved views ship as an internal beta behind a feature flag.
  2. Commitment is 18 points: BILL-412 (5), SEARCH-188 (3), SEARCH-201 (8), PLAT-77 (2). Buffer is 4 points against 22 available.
  3. SEARCH-210 and ADMIN-54 are not in this sprint. They return to the backlog without a promised date.
  4. Shared views do not leave the flag until Elena confirms view-created, view-applied, and view-revoked events in staging.
  5. No production deploys on Thursday, November 26 or Friday, November 27. Next planned production window is Wednesday, December 2.
  6. Customer-facing export errors must name the file and the attempt time. Generic “try again” copy is out of scope for the fix.
  7. Sprint review is Thursday, December 3, 2:00–2:45 p.m. PT. Priya will send the invite today.

6. Open questions

  • Will the payments sandbox reset actually land Wednesday, November 25, or should verification of BILL-412 slip to the week of December 1?
  • What is the exact internal beta cohort for shared views — the design partners list, or a smaller slice of the support team?
  • Does revoke on a shared view need to notify the people currently using it, or is a silent removal acceptable for v1?
  • Should the 50% ticket-reduction target be measured against all “export failed” tags, or only recurring scheduled exports?
  • Is Nina’s design review of SEARCH-201 required before the flag can open, or can Marcus sign off in her absence?
  • Do we need a customer-facing status page note if Wednesday’s sandbox work causes a brief staging-only outage, or is internal comms enough?

Open questions stay on this list until an owner answers them in the sprint channel. Unresolved items will be reviewed at standup on Tuesday, November 24.
